title: Stable score units and runtime toggle for similarity behavior
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Rerank and similarity consumers observe inconsistent scoring units across clients and runtimes. Some clients assume dot-product units, others expect cosine in [-1,1], and earlier server behavior implicitly normalized vectors for some models. This ambiguity causes regression risk when models, quantization, or runtime batching change vector norms. It also makes thresholding and A/B evaluation error-prone.

Goal: Provide a clear, testable contract for similarity scores, a low-risk compatibility path for legacy clients, and a runtime-configurable toggle for safe migration. We must avoid per-request heavy transforms that hurt latency or batching, and offer deterministic, measurable behavior for rerank endpoints and scoring telemetry.
proposal:
1) Introduce a stable score unit called 'score_units' that is explicit in the rerank API response metadata and in request headers. Two supported units at launch: 'cosine' (range -1..1) and 'dot' (raw dot-product).
2) Implement a lightweight runtime toggle (header: X-Redwood-Score-Mode) with values: 'legacy' (current behavior), 'cosine' (server normalizes vectors before scoring), 'dot' (no normalization). The default for new clients will be 'cosine'.
3) Provide a compatibility shim: when X-Redwood-Score-Mode=legacy, server preserves existing pre-1.22 behavior (including any historical normalization heuristics) and emits a deprecation warning in response headers.
4) Avoid copying or re-encoding cached KV pages per-request: implement normalization pipeline that operates on cached embeddings once on write/ingest (background job) and on-demand with an async fallback to preserve latency.
5) Add deterministic per-request validation that refuses combinations that are ambiguous (e.g., model variants with different embedding scales) and responds with diagnostic hints.
6) Ship client migration guide, test harness, and a telemetry dashboard showing score distribution shifts by clients and models.
tasks: Add X-Redwood-Score-Mode header parsing to API gateway and surface in request context
Implement score_units field in rerank response schema and update OpenAPI spec
Add normalization-on-ingest path for embeddings store with async backfill job
Implement server-side fast-normalize routine optimized for batching and quantized kernels
Expose runtime flag to enable/disable legacy shim per tenant for gradual rollout
Add end-to-end rerank regression tests (unit + integration) covering cosine vs dot behaviors
Create migration guide and sample client patch for JS/Python SDKs
Add telemetry: histogram of raw dot scores, cosine scores, and per-client delta metrics
Benchmark latency/regression with 128/512 dim embeddings under high QPS and batching
Create canary rollout plan and automated safety checks before global flip
acceptance_criteria: API accepts X-Redwood-Score-Mode and returns score_units in rerank responses
Default mode for new tenants is 'cosine' and documented in quickstart
Legacy mode reproduces pre-1.22 scoring for a canonical test vector set within epsilon
Normalization is implemented without increasing p50 latency by >5% for 95th percentile batching profile
Backfill job successfully normalizes historical cached embeddings for a test tenant within expected window
SDK patches available and example migration notebook that demonstrates parity between 'legacy' and migrated clients
Telemetry shows stable distribution and an alert triggers if score distribution shifts by >10% during rollout
